subject: Clarify hosted API price slabs & invoicing for high-throughput PoC
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmerobotics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmerobotics.com>, procurement@acmerobotics.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Hosted API pricing bands for expected 1B tokens/mo

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked good for our batch reranking workload. Before we commit to a month-long PoC I need two quick things to take to procurement: a simple price table that shows baseline per-token pricing at a few commitment tiers, and a short note on how overages are billed.

Our rough target for the PoC is ~1B tokens/month with occasional spikes to 1.5B. For the annual rollout we expect to be north of 3B tokens/month. Can you provide:
- The effective per-1k-token list price for hosted API at: 0–500M, 500M–2B, >2B tokens/mo
- Any additional discounts for a 12‑month committed spend (and whether unused commit converts to credits)
- Overage pricing rules and whether we can set a hard cap or auto-burst policy
- Whether reserved concurrency or Dedicated pools are required to get the lower tiers

Procurement also asked whether invoices can be net-45 and if you have a standard SOW template. We can sign NDA/PO once costs are clear.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of ML Platforms, Acme Robotics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing bands for expected 1B tokens/mo

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise table we typically share for hosted API. I'm attaching the full PDF with examples and billing terms. Let me know if you'd like this in Excel.

Redwood hosted API — illustrative effective pricing (per 1k tokens):
- 0–500M/mo: $0.020 per 1k tokens (list)
- 500M–2B/mo: $0.013 per 1k tokens (banded discount applied on consumption within band)
- >2B/mo: $0.0085 per 1k tokens (requires committed monthly credit)

Committed 12‑month discount: additional 10–18% depending on commit size (applies to >500M band). Unused committed credits convert to rolling credits for 90 days by default; longer credit expiry negotiable on enterprise contracts.

Overage rules: overages billed at the next band rate; you can set a hard cap that prevents token consumption beyond your commit (we'll return 429s) or enable an auto-burst policy which permits short bursts at an elevated rate and overage billing. Both are configured per-route.

Reserved concurrency: Not required for these price bands on hosted API, but for sustained low-latency at peak QPS we recommend Dedicated pools (separate agreement) — they include SLA credits and predictable concurrency.

Invoice terms: we support net-30 by default; net-45 is possible for enterprise deals (procurement routing/credit check required). I'll loop in Ben for anything outside standard terms.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-price-slabs-v2.pdf

Next step: can we do a 30-minute pricing review with procurement next week? Proposed times: Tue/Thu morning PST.

Best,
Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmerobotics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmerobotics.com>, procurement@acmerobotics.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:46:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing bands for expected 1B tokens/mo

Karthik — quick follow ups from procurement:
1) For the >2B tier you listed "requires committed monthly credit" — do you allow ramp phasing over first 3 months? Our traffic will be steady but grows over Q1.
2) Is the banded discount applied only to tokens inside the band, or is it volume-tier pricing (all tokens at the tier rate once threshold crossed)?
3) Would Redwood accept a PO and 45-day invoice with ACH payment?

Also, Samantha asked whether we can get a sample SOW that lists support SLAs for PoC.

Thanks — DP

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmerobotics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@acmerobotics.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 12:07:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing bands for expected 1B tokens/mo

Hi Daniel — quick answers inline: 

1) Ramp phasing: yes. We generally allow a 60–90 day phasing window for large commitments (we'll draft a schedule in the SOW). During the ramp you pay at the committed band pro‑rata; once steady state is reached the full committed credits apply.

2) Pricing model: banded (marginal) pricing — you pay each band's rate for consumption within that band. We can offer an alternative "volume-tier" (all tokens at the higher discount) as an option for very large deals; that would typically require a minimum annual spend guarantee.

3) PO + net-45 ACH: acceptable pending credit onboarding. We'll send a standard PO/contract packet and a draft SOW.

Additional note on SLOs: Hosted API includes latency guidance but SLA credits are reserved for Dedicated. For the PoC, we can include a PoC support addendum (four business hour response, dedicated Slack channel).

I'll attach a PO-terms-draft and a templated SOW. If you want a deeper concession (e.g., extra 3% off list) we'll need an approver sign-off — looping Marissa for visibility.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Ben/Karthik — approved a one-time commercial concession to assist the PoC: additional 5% off the >500M band for the first 3 months of the PoC (applies to metered consumption within that band), contingent on a signed PO and a 12-month intent note. Procurement can accept net-45 ACH for this arrangement.

Action items:
- Karthik: send updated PDF and the PO-terms-draft to procurement (attached).

I'll also add a short clause to the SOW draft about ramp phasing and credit expiry.

Thanks — Marissa

VP, Sales
